title: How NASA Trapped Speeding Comet Dust
description: In 1999, NASA launched Stardust to trap cometary grains using ultra-low-density aerogel. Seven years later, the probe delivered pristine samples back to Earth.

beats.text: NASA caught speeding comet dust inside ultra-low-density silica aerogel.
beats.visual: Stardust aerogel sample collection grid displaying translucent tiles, 1999

beats.text: Launched in 1999, Stardust traveled three billion miles over seven years.
beats.visual: Delta II rocket launching the Stardust spacecraft from Cape Canaveral, 1999
queries: Delta II Stardust launch Cape Canaveral

beats.text: To capture particles without destroying them on impact, engineers deployed a collector tray shaped like a tennis racket.
beats.visual: Stardust spacecraft deploying its tennis-racket shaped collector tray, artist illustration, 1999

beats.text: In January 2004, the spacecraft swept past Comet Wild 2 to gently catch microscopic cosmic grains.
beats.visual: Close-up photograph of the nucleus of Comet Wild 2 taken by Stardust, 2004

beats.text: On January 15, 2006, its sample return capsule descended under parachutes directly into the Utah desert.
